clue.text: Cheer 9 flying this?

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 9 across

explanation.surface: A crowd might cheer a pilot doing stunts in some aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the cheer and pilot are shuffled into HELICOPTER, and a pilot flying one is exactly what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter is an aircraft a pilot flies, so the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: Time to rise and renounce Catholic faith

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from bottom to top
to renounce something is to give it up, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: an epoch is a period of time
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: A lapsed believer gets up one morning and abandons the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: EPOCH read upwards is HCOPE; take out the C and HOPE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope, as in faith, hope and charity, is a trust or confidence in something unseen.

clue.text: Car accessories in vinyl – nearly brand new

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
the latest thing is brand new

explanation.surface: A new car's trim is finished in nearly-new vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the red L signs a British learner driver must display; 'in' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: L-plates are signs attached to a car driven by a learner, so they are accessories for a car.

clue.text: Possible ingredient of snack box containing too much corn

indicators.note: the box word holds the next idea inside it

blocks.note: a cage is a box to confine something
OTT is short for over the top
corn in the sense of trite sentiment is cheese, as in cheesy

explanation.surface: A lunch box crammed with sweetcorn suggests a snack's ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corn' looks like the vegetable but means hackneyed sentimentality, which is also called cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage cheese is a soft curd cheese that might go into a snack such as a sandwich.

clue.text: Washington taking against following games in particular

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside
coming after means this part is placed second in the build

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school games
Washington DC, the US capital
anti means against

explanation.surface: Washington opposes the games, in a specific respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' looks like a person or a state but is the US capital, Washington DC; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular person is fussy about details, which is what being pedantic means.

clue.text: Take off two heads, the first being uncovered

indicators.note: uncovering strips away the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, the first of two heads
a cape is a headland, the second of the two heads

explanation.surface: Someone removes two heads, the first one left bare.
explanation.walkthrough: The two heads are headlands, NESS and CAPE; the first is uncovered to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off is to flee or run away, which is what escape means.

clue.text: What poisonous gas goes round where flights begin?

indicators.note: going round turns the pair to face the other way

blocks.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
CO is carbon monoxide

explanation.surface: A question about what toxic gas circulates at an airport departure point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flights' suggests aircraft, but these are the feathered flights on darts; the oche is the line a darts player throws from.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the throwing line in darts, so the dart's flights start their journey there.

clue.text: Pen with another farm animal needing service

blocks.note: a cow is a farm animal
a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: A pen holding a second farm animal needs some attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like an enclosure for the farm animal but is the verb to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-write is to author a work jointly with another person.

clue.text: Stretching, Noel got in a muddle?

indicators.note: letters in a muddle are jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Was Noel's yoga stretching session a confusing tangle?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'in a muddle' is part of the fodder as well as the indicator phrase reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongation is the act of lengthening something, which is stretching it.

clue.text: Speculative root of negative breaking story

indicators.note: breaking into something means going inside it

blocks.note: the plot is the storyline
i is the square root of minus one in mathematics

explanation.surface: A speculative root of some negative thing interrupts a narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root of negative' looks like a first-letter instruction giving N, but it is mathematical: the square root of minus one is i.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot scheme is a trial run, so pilot as an adjective means experimental or speculative.

clue.text: Fake UN agency's series of fourteen stars?

blocks.note: to doctor something is to falsify it
the World Health Organization is a UN agency

explanation.surface: A bogus United Nations body runs a series featuring a constellation of fourteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen stars are the actors who have played the Doctor in the long-running BBC science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who is a television series whose title role has been played by many lead actors.

clue.text: Anxious after missing intro, don't record catchy tunes

indicators.note: missing the intro means losing the opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to enter data is to record it
a hook is a catchy musical phrase

explanation.surface: A nervous musician begs a producer not to record catchy songs without an intro.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase don't enter loses its first letter, then hooks follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on tenterhooks is an idiom for being in a state of nervous suspense.

clue.text: Running without effort, moving quietly to the last activity of the line

indicators.note: the soft-music letter is shifted from the front to the end of its word
without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around another

blocks.note: trotting is running at a gentle pace
to take pains is to make an effort

explanation.surface: Someone jogs effortlessly, moving quietly to the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Quietly is p (piano) in music, and here it names the letter that moves to the end of the effort word. 'Without' has its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotting is the hobby of logging locomotives seen from beside the railway line.

clue.text: Craving for dessert that's small and dry, in truth

indicators.note: in means these parts sit inside the next word

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for small
TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink
sooth is an old word for truth, as in soothsayer

explanation.surface: An appetite for pudding that's modest and without wine, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' suggests a wine, but it means teetotal, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet tooth is a liking for sugary food such as desserts.

clue.text: Lead dropped from disaster movie – one with a plant

indicators.note: dropping the lead means losing the front letter

blocks.note: Twister is a 1996 disaster film about tornadoes
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: The star leaves a disaster film; someone else takes over with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the star actor of the film, but here it is the title's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing plant with drooping purple flower clusters.

clue.text: What's splintered after playing cricket, say?

indicators.note: after places the first idea behind the second in the answer

blocks.note: a side that is in is batting, its turn to play
a sect is a group that has splintered off a larger body

explanation.surface: Something is left in splinters after a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' looks like the game, linked to playing and splintered bats, but it is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a jumping, chirping creature, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Indian, say, to select a route

blocks.note: to take is to choose
taken as written
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone from India is asked to pick a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person, but it is a curry meal; in Britain an Indian is a common takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway is a meal bought ready-made to eat at home, and Indian food is a typical example.

clue.text: Rude sound when husband shifts

indicators.note: a letter that shifts leaves its spot and goes in elsewhere

blocks.note: hearty means sound, in good health
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband changing position makes an impolite noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but means healthy; the H at the front moves to the next-to-last position.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and frank about bodily matters, so earthy can mean rude.

clue.text: Windows perhaps beneath covering – e.g. brick screen

indicators.note: in a down entry, beneath puts this part below the others

blocks.note: re means about or covering a subject
brick red is an example of the colour
Windows is an example of an operating system

explanation.surface: Windows sit under a cladding of brick screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' with a capital is Microsoft's operating system, OS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Battle to weaken throne

blocks.note: to water down is to weaken
throne is slang for a toilet, the loo

explanation.surface: A fight to undermine a monarch's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' suggests a monarch, but it is jokey slang for the toilet; loo is the British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is the 1815 battle where Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: Circuit to secure transformer?

blocks.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
to lace up is to fasten or secure

explanation.surface: Wiring a circuit to hold an electrical transformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit' and 'transformer' suggest electronics, but the transformer is the mathematician behind the Laplace transform.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Simon Laplace devised the Laplace transform, so he is jokingly a transformer.

clue.text: City hosting key marketplace?

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A city plays host to an important market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is Venice's historic commercial district, so a marketplace; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Instruction for MPs while their pen wavers

indicators.note: something that wavers is unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament get orders as their pens hesitate over a document.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-line whip is a party's strictest order to its MPs to vote, underlined three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip is a party directive to Members of Parliament ordering attendance and a vote.

clue.text: Writing about one's girl

indicators.note: about means around, so one part surrounds the other

blocks.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
I for one, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A note written about someone's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I, so one's becomes I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is a young unmarried woman, a girl.

clue.text: Part of order somehow folded down

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: Part of an order got folded down in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a fraternal friendly society, so an Oddfellow is a member of that order.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oddfellow is a member of the Independent Order of Oddfellows, a mutual-aid fraternity.

clue.text: Like some sultanas from an impaired box?

indicators.note: a box holds things inside, so the answer is enclosed in the words before

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Dried fruit taken from a damaged box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sultanas' looks like the dried grapes, but here they are wives of sultans; Oman is ruled by a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultanas are the wives of sultans, and some are from Oman, the Gulf sultanate.

clue.text: Enjoys hot mess

blocks.note: to have something is to enjoy it, as in enjoying good health
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone relishes a warm jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a hash of something is to make a mess of it.

clue.text: Materials using unusual prose style

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Writing materials that employ an odd literary manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyesters are synthetic fabrics, a kind of material.
